title: Read-repair race causing missing debits during autoscale surge
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a recent autoscaling event in eu-west-1 we observed a short period where per-key debits were undercounted, allowing a small set of clients to exceed their quota for ~20s. Root cause appears to be a race between the read-repair path that consolidates sparse shard segments and the fast path that applies debits during autoscale-driven shard handoff. This ticket tracks the investigation, reproducible test, proposed fixes, and rollout plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy local dev cluster with shard-aggregator configured to split small segments (use config flag: aggregator.split_threshold=500ms).
2) Seed a single API key with low burst credits and start steady traffic at 8 QPS per key.
3) Trigger autoscale by simulating a spike of write traffic (use scripts/autoscale-surge.sh).
4) Observe aggregator logs and token accounting: look for reorder of read-repair flushes and apply-debit RPC where the flush overwrites a recent in-memory debit snapshot.
5) Confirm behavior by checking meter snapshots on both old and new shard owners and the global ledger.
hypothesis: When a shard is rebalanced during autoscale, the aggressive read-repair consolidation runs concurrently with in-flight debit application. The read-repair path writes merged segment state back to object storage and triggers a lightweight snapshot replay on the new owner. If the apply-debit RPC from the fast path arrives between the storage write and the replayer's merge, the replayer may replay an older merged state that lacks the most recent debits, resulting in a temporary under-debit window. This is exacerbated by the aggregator's eventual reconciliation heuristics which delay corrective re-debits until periodic reconciliation (~30s).
proposed_fix: Short term: add a conservative in-memory timestamp check on shard handoff to serialize the final in-memory debit flush before releasing the handoff lease. Medium term: change read-repair to use a compare-and-merge protocol that includes last-applied-seq numbers for debits and rejects merges that would regress last-applied. Long term: add a fast reconciliation hook that runs immediately after handoff with bounded correction (idempotent replays capped to N tokens per-key) to avoid both under- and over-debiting.
testing_plan: Unit tests for compare-and-merge semantics in aggregator (covering seq holes and duplicates).
Integration test that simulates autoscale handoff with instrumented timing to force the race. This lives in infra/tests/aggregator_autoscale_repro.go and will run in CI-nightly before merging.
Canary rollout to eu-west-1 with metric guard rails (throttle-rate, per-key-unmetered-spike) and automatic rollback if per-key over-allow > 0.1% for 5m.
Add synthetic load dashboards to monitor 'per_key_debit_gap' derived metric and alert on >0.5 tokens gap across shards.
